_note: Hand-curated domain notes. The agent must surface these verbatim when the airport appears in an answer; it must not invent new ones.

SNA.note: John Wayne Airport operates under a court-ordered noise and access agreement that caps annual passenger volume and regulated commercial departures, with a night-time curfew. Congestion here is a legal ceiling, not a physical one — extra terminal capacity cannot lift it.

ANC.note: Anchorage is one of the world's largest cargo hubs. Passenger-only metrics understate its role and its investment case; freight tonnage is the more relevant driver.

LGA.note: LaGuardia is FAA slot-controlled and subject to a perimeter rule, so departures cannot grow freely with demand.

DCA.note: Reagan National is FAA slot-controlled with a statutory perimeter rule; new service requires congressional or FAA action.

JFK.note: JFK is FAA slot-controlled. Departure growth is administratively limited regardless of terminal capacity.

EWR.note: Newark is FAA slot-controlled following sustained delay problems.

ORD.note: O'Hare completed a runway reconfiguration programme; airfield capacity has been expanded more recently than terminal capacity.
